records.source: וַתִּשְׁלַם֙ כָּל־הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑הסוַיָּבֵ֨א שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אֶת־קָדְשֵׁ֣י׀דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֗יו וְאֶת־הַכֶּ֤סֶף וְאֶת־הַזָּהָב֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֔ים נָתַ֕ן בְּאֹצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And was complete all the work which did Solomon for [the] house of Yahweh; and brought Solomon [the] holy things of David his father, and the silver and the gold and all the vessels he put in [the] treasuries of [the] house of the God.
pieces: So all the work that Solomon did on the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was finished. Then Solomon brought in the things his father David had dedicated, and he put the silver, the gold and all the vessels in the treasuries of the house of God.

L.1: And all the work that Solomon did for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was complete. And Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father, and the silver and the gold and all the vessels he put in the treasuries of the house of God.

R.1: When Solomon had finished all the work on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, he brought in the gifts his father David had set apart for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He put the silver, the gold and all the other objects in the storerooms of God's temple.

decisions.choice: told also in 1 Kings 7:51
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 1 Kings 7:51 almost word for word. There the work is that of "King Solomon" and the vessels go into the treasuries of "the house of Yahweh"; here it is "Solomon", the list reads "all the vessels", and the treasuries are those of "the house of God".

decisions.choice: holy things of David: what David had dedicated to Yahweh
decisions.reason: David set apart for Yahweh the silver and gold he took in his wars and received as gifts (1 Chronicles 18:11; 22:14; 29:2-5).

decisions.choice: and the silver ... he put: the silver, gold and vessels are what David dedicated
decisions.reason: Each item is marked as an object and joined by "and", and the verb "he put" follows them. The silver, gold and vessels are the dedicated things themselves, which Solomon stored in the treasuries.

decisions.choice: dedicated (Balanced); gifts ... set apart; storerooms; temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:51: Balanced says "dedicated" for "the holy things" (m2), and Readable says "gifts ... set apart", "storerooms" for the treasuries and "temple" for the house.

records.heading: The ark is brought into the temple

records.source: אָז֩ יַקְהֵ֨יל שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אֶת־זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְאֶת־כָּל־רָאשֵׁ֨י הַמַּטּ֜וֹת נְשִׂיאֵ֧י הָאָב֛וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לְֽהַעֲל֞וֹת אֶת־אֲר֧וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֛ה מֵעִ֥יר דָּוִ֖יד הִ֥יא צִיּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Then assembled Solomon [the] elders of Israel and all [the] heads of the tribes, [the] leaders of the fathers of [the] sons of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh from [the] city of David, that [is] Zion.
pieces: Then Solomon called together to Jerusalem the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral families of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They were to bring the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} up from the city of David, that is, Zion.

L.2: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the city of David, which [is] Zion.

R.2: Then Solomon called the leaders of Israel to come to Jerusalem. These were the elders, the heads of all the tribes, and the leaders of the families of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They were to bring the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} up to the temple from the city of David, which is also called Zion.

decisions.choice: told also in 1 Kings 8:1
decisions.reason: Verses 2-10 follow 1 Kings 8:1-9 closely. Here the leaders are gathered "to Jerusalem" where Kings has "to King Solomon [in] Jerusalem", and "and" joins the elders to the heads of the tribes.

decisions.choice: bring up the ark from the city of David: carry it up to the new house on the higher ground
decisions.reason: David had brought the ark into his city and set it in a tent he pitched for it (1 Chronicles 15:1; 16:1). The house stood on the hill just north of the old city, on Mount Moriah, where David had bought the threshing floor of Ornan (3:1), so the ark goes "up".

decisions.choice: Zion: here the old fortress city of David
decisions.reason: Zion first named the stronghold David captured (1 Chronicles 11:5). Later the name was used for the temple hill and for all Jerusalem, but here it is explained as the city of David, the older part below the temple.

decisions.choice: the leaders of the fathers: the heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: "Fathers" is short for "houses of the fathers", the family groups within each tribe (Numbers 1:2; 7:2).

decisions.choice: up to the temple; also called Zion (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 8:1, Readable says where the ark was going, which the next verses make clear, and explains that Zion is another name for the city of David.

records.source: וַיִּקָּהֲל֧וּ אֶל־הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ כָּל־אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּחָ֑ג ה֖וּא הַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִעִֽי׃
records.gloss: And assembled to the king all [the] men of Israel at the festival; it [was] the month the seventh.
pieces: All the men of Israel gathered before the king at the festival, which was in the seventh month.

L.3: And all the men of Israel assembled to the king at the festival; that [was] the seventh month.

R.3: All the men of Israel came to the king at the time of the Festival of Booths, in the seventh month of the year.

decisions.choice: told also in 1 Kings 8:2, without the month's old name
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 8:2 reads "to King Solomon in the month of Ethanim, at the festival". Chronicles has "to the king" and leaves out the old name Ethanim, so that "it was the seventh month" now follows "the festival" directly.

decisions.choice: the festival: the Festival of Booths
decisions.reason: The great pilgrim festival of the seventh month was the Festival of Booths, held for seven days from the fifteenth day of the month (Leviticus 23:34-36; Deuteronomy 16:13-15). 2 Chronicles 7:8-10 tells how the dedication and the festival were kept together, and the people were sent home on the twenty-third day of the month.

decisions.choice: all the men of Israel: Israel gathered as a people
decisions.reason: The phrase stands for the nation as a whole. At the pilgrim festivals the men were required to come (Deuteronomy 16:16), though whole families also came (Deuteronomy 16:14).

decisions.choice: the Festival of Booths (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names the festival that the Hebrew calls simply "the festival", as in 1 Kings 8:2.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ כֹּ֖ל זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ הַלְוִיִּ֖ם אֶת־הָאָרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And came all [the] elders of Israel, and lifted up the Levites the ark.
pieces: When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the Levites picked up the ark.

L.4: And all the elders of Israel came, and the Levites lifted up the ark.

R.4: When all the elders of Israel had come, the Levites lifted the ark onto their shoulders.

decisions.choice: the Levites lifted up the ark: 1 Kings 8:3 says "the priests"
decisions.reason: The sentence is the same as 1 Kings 8:3 except for who lifts the ark. Chronicles names the Levites, the tribe the law chose to carry it (Deuteronomy 10:8; 1 Chronicles 15:2, 15). The priests were Levites too, and in verse 7 it is the priests who take the ark into the inner room, where only priests could go.

decisions.choice: lifted up the ark: carried it by its poles, as the law required
decisions.reason: The ark was to be carried on the shoulders by its poles (Numbers 7:9; 1 Chronicles 15:15). David's first attempt to move it on a cart ended in Uzzah's death (1 Chronicles 13:7-10).

decisions.choice: onto their shoulders (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says how the ark was lifted, as in 1 Kings 8:3, since it was carried on poles and never pulled on a cart.

records.source: וַיַּעֲל֤וּ אֶת־הָאָרוֹן֙ וְאֶת־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְאֶת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֥י הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּאֹ֑הֶל הֶעֱל֣וּ אֹתָ֔ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים הַלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: And brought up the ark and [the] tent of meeting and all [the] vessels of the holiness which [were] in the tent; brought up them the priests the Levites.
pieces: They brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy utensils that were in the tent. The Levitical priests carried them up.

L.5: And they brought up the ark and the tent of meeting and all the holy vessels that [were] in the tent; the priests, the Levites, brought them up.

R.5: They brought up the ark, the meeting tent, and all the holy objects that were in the tent. The priests, who were from the tribe of Levi, carried them up.

decisions.choice: told also in 1 Kings 8:4, with "the priests, the Levites"
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 8:4 reads "the ark of Yahweh" and "the priests and the Levites". Chronicles has "the ark" and "the priests, the Levites", with no "and".

decisions.choice: the priests, the Levites: the priests who come from the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: Without "and", the two words name one group, as in Deuteronomy's "the priests, the Levites" (Deuteronomy 17:9; 18:1). Some Hebrew manuscripts and the early Greek translation read "and", as 1 Kings 8:4 does, which would make two groups, the priests helped by the Levites of verse 4. The text as it stands is followed here.

decisions.choice: the tent of meeting: the tent from the wilderness, which had stood at Gibeon
alternatives: the tent David set up for the ark in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Chronicles says that the tent of meeting Moses made stood at the high place at Gibeon (1:3). It may instead be the tent David pitched for the ark in Jerusalem (1:4; 1 Chronicles 16:1), as noted at 1 Kings 8:4. Either way, the old place of worship is brought into the new house.

decisions.choice: the holy vessels: the utensils used in worship
decisions.reason: The word covers all the equipment of the sanctuary, such as bowls, dishes and lampstands (Numbers 3:31; 4:15).

decisions.choice: Levitical priests (Balanced); the meeting tent; holy objects; from the tribe of Levi (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "Levitical priests" and Readable "the priests, who were from the tribe of Levi", as in Deuteronomy 17:9. Readable uses "meeting tent" and "objects" as in 1 Kings 8:4.

records.source: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וְכָל־עֲדַ֧ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הַנּוֹעָדִ֥ים עָלָ֖יו לִפְנֵ֣י הָאָר֑וֹן מְזַבְּחִים֙ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יִסָּפְר֛וּ וְלֹ֥א יִמָּנ֖וּ מֵרֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And the king Solomon and all [the] congregation of Israel, those gathered to him, [were] before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that not were counted and not were numbered from abundance.
pieces: King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel who had gathered to him were in front of the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that they could not be counted or numbered.

L.6: And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who had gathered to him [were] before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or numbered for abundance.

R.6: King Solomon and the whole community of Israel that had come together around him were in front of the ark. They sacrificed so many sheep and cattle that no one could count them.

decisions.choice: told also in 1 Kings 8:5
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 1 Kings 8:5 except that Chronicles leaves out "with him" after "gathered to him".

decisions.choice: sacrificing: offering sacrifices as the ark was moved
decisions.reason: When David brought the ark into his city, sacrifices were offered along the way (1 Chronicles 15:26; 16:1). Here the whole gathering does the same on a vast scale.

decisions.choice: not counted and not numbered: far too many to count
decisions.reason: The two verbs say the same thing twice for emphasis, as in 1 Kings 8:5.

decisions.choice: community (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses "community" for the congregation, as in the books before.

records.source: וַיָּבִ֣יאוּ הַ֠כֹּהֲנִים אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֧ה אֶל־מְקוֹמ֛וֹ אֶל־דְּבִ֥יר הַבַּ֖יִת אֶל־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקְּדָשִׁ֑ים אֶל־תַּ֖חַת כַּנְפֵ֥י הַכְּרוּבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And brought the priests [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh to its place, to [the] inner sanctuary of the house, to [the] holy of the holies, to under [the] wings of the cherubim.
pieces: The priests then carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} into its place in the inner sanctuary of the house, the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubim.

L.7: And the priests brought the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to its place, into the inner room of the house, into the holy of holies, under the wings of the cherubim.

R.7: The priests carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the place prepared for it. They took it into the inner room of the temple, the most holy place, and set it under the wings of the cherubim.

decisions.choice: told also in 1 Kings 8:6, word for word; the priests take the ark in
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is the same as 1 Kings 8:6. The Levites had carried the ark (verse 4), but only the priests could enter the most holy place, so they bring it to its place (Numbers 4:5, 15).

decisions.choice: the inner sanctuary: the innermost room at the back of the house
decisions.reason: This is the room Solomon built for the ark, twenty cubits each way, also called the most holy place (3:8).

decisions.choice: holy of holies: the most holy place
decisions.reason: Hebrew makes a superlative by joining a noun to its own plural: "the holy of holies" is the holiest place of all, as in the tabernacle (Exodus 26:33-34).

decisions.choice: the cherubim: the two great winged figures Solomon set in the inner room
decisions.reason: These are the two cherubim overlaid with gold whose wings reached from wall to wall (3:10-13). They are not the two small cherubim on the ark's cover (Exodus 25:18-20).

decisions.choice: house (Literal, Balanced); temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 8:6, Literal and Balanced keep "house" and Readable says "temple". Literal and Readable call the room "the inner room" and Balanced "the inner sanctuary".

records.source: וַיִּהְי֤וּ הַכְּרוּבִים֙ פֹּרְשִׂ֣ים כְּנָפַ֔יִם עַל־מְק֖וֹם הָאָר֑וֹן וַיְכַסּ֧וּ הַכְּרוּבִ֛ים עַל־הָאָר֥וֹן וְעַל־בַּדָּ֖יו מִלְמָֽעְלָה׃
records.gloss: And were the cherubim spreading wings over [the] place of the ark, and covered the cherubim over the ark and over its poles from above.
pieces: The cherubim spread their wings over the place where the ark stood, and so the cherubim formed a covering above the ark and its poles.

L.8: And the cherubim were spreading [their] wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim made a covering over the ark and over its poles from above.

R.8: The wings of the cherubim were spread out over the place where the ark was. So their wings formed a cover over the ark and the poles used to carry it.

decisions.choice: told also in 1 Kings 8:7, with small differences
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 8:7 begins "For the cherubim were spreading" and has the wings spread "toward" the place of the ark; Chronicles begins "And the cherubim were" and has "over". For "covered" Chronicles uses a different verb from Kings, with the same sense.

decisions.choice: its poles: the carrying poles fixed in rings on the sides of the ark
decisions.reason: The poles were to stay in their rings and never be taken out (Exodus 25:13-15).

decisions.choice: the poles used to carry it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the poles were for, as in 1 Kings 8:7.

records.source: וַֽיַּאֲרִיכוּ֮ הַבַּדִּים֒ וַיֵּרָאוּ֩ רָאשֵׁ֨י הַבַּדִּ֤ים מִן־הָאָרוֹן֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַדְּבִ֔יר וְלֹ֥א יֵרָא֖וּ הַח֑וּצָה וַֽיְהִי־שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And were long the poles, and were seen [the] heads of the poles from the ark on [the] face of the inner sanctuary, and not were seen outside; and it is there until the day the this.
pieces: The poles were so long that their ends, reaching out from the ark, could be seen in front of the inner sanctuary, though not from outside. It is still there to this day.

L.9: And the poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the ark in front of the inner room, but they were not seen outside; and it is there to this day.

R.9: The poles were so long that their ends, reaching out from the ark, could be seen in front of the inner room. But no one outside could see them. It is still there to this day.

decisions.choice: told also in 1 Kings 8:8, with "from the ark" and "it is there"
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 8:8 says the ends of the poles were seen "from the holy place" and "they are there". Chronicles says "from the ark" and "it is there".

decisions.choice: from the ark: the ends of the poles stuck out from the ark toward the front of the inner room
alternatives: seen from the ark, that is, from where the ark stood
decisions.reason: The phrase most naturally says where the ends of the poles came from: they reached out from the ark far enough to be noticed at the front of the inner room. 1 Kings 8:8 instead says where they could be seen from, the holy place.

decisions.choice: it is there: the ark, or the poles with it
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, so it most likely means the ark itself, though it may refer to the poles taken together. 1 Kings 8:8 has the plural, "they are there".

decisions.choice: to this day: the day of the source the writer used
decisions.reason: This is the first time 2 Chronicles uses the phrase. Chronicles was written after the exile (36:22-23), when the temple had been burned and the ark was gone (36:19). The words come over from the account in 1 Kings 8:8, written while the temple still stood, and the writer kept them as he found them.

decisions.choice: reaching out from the ark (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "from the ark" means, following m2. Every level keeps "to this day", as throughout Samuel, Kings and Chronicles.

records.source: אֵ֚ין בָּֽאָר֔וֹן רַ֚ק שְׁנֵ֣י הַלֻּח֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּחֹרֵ֑ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּרַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ עִם־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃פ
records.gloss: Nothing [was] in the ark only [the] two tablets which put Moses at Horeb, where made Yahweh with [the] sons of Israel in their coming out from Egypt.
pieces: The ark held nothing but the two tablets Moses had put in it at Horeb, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made a covenant with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} after they came out of Egypt.

L.10: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had put [there] at Horeb, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made [a covenant] with the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel when they came out of Egypt.

R.10: The only things inside the ark were the two tablets that Moses had put there at Mount Horeb. That was where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made a covenant with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} after they came out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: told also in 1 Kings 8:9, slightly shorter
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 8:9 reads "the two tablets of stone that Moses placed there" and "out of the land of Egypt". Chronicles has "the two tablets that Moses put" and "out of Egypt". The two tablets are those of the Ten Commandments, which Moses put in the ark (Deuteronomy 10:1-5).

decisions.choice: made [a covenant]: "covenant" is understood
decisions.reason: The verb means "cut" and is the regular verb for making a covenant. Here the word "covenant" is left unsaid, as in 1 Kings 8:9, but the tablets were the covenant's written terms (Deuteronomy 9:9-11).

decisions.choice: Horeb: the mountain also called Sinai
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy uses Horeb for the mountain where the covenant was made (Deuteronomy 5:2), which Exodus usually calls Sinai.

decisions.choice: [there] (Literal); Mount Horeb (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies where Moses put the tablets. Readable adds "Mount" so that the name is not taken for a town, as in 1 Kings 8:9.

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י בְּצֵ֥את הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים מִן־הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ כִּ֠י כָּל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים הַֽנִּמְצְאִים֙ הִתְקַדָּ֔שׁוּ אֵ֖ין לִשְׁמ֥וֹר לְמַחְלְקֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And it was, in [the] coming out of the priests from the holy [place], for all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves, [there was] not keeping to divisions,
pieces: Then the priests came out of the holy place. All the priests who were present had consecrated themselves, whatever their division.

L.11: And it happened, when the priests came out from the holy [place], for all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves, without keeping to [their] divisions,

R.11: Then the priests came out of the holy place. All the priests who were there had made themselves holy for this day, not only those whose group was on duty.

decisions.choice: verses 11-13 add to 1 Kings 8:10
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 8:10 says simply that when the priests came out of the holy place, the cloud filled the house. Chronicles opens the same way, then tells of the priests, the singers and the music (verses 11-13) before the cloud comes.

decisions.choice: one long sentence: "when the priests came out ..." finds its main clause at the end of verse 13
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins "And it happened, when the priests came out", then stops to describe the priests (verse 11) and the singers and trumpeters (verse 12), and only in verse 13 says what happened: the house was filled with a cloud.

decisions.choice: consecrated themselves without keeping to their divisions: every priest present took part, not only the group on duty
decisions.reason: David divided the priests into twenty-four groups that served in turn (1 Chronicles 24:1-19). For this day every priest who was there had made himself ready, so the rota was set aside. Compare 30:3, where not enough priests had consecrated themselves.

decisions.choice: the holy place: the sanctuary where they had set the ark
decisions.reason: The priests had gone into the inner sanctuary to set the ark in place (verse 7), as in 1 Kings 8:10.

decisions.choice: full sentences (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the long sentence of verses 11-13 and ends this verse with a comma. Balanced and Readable break it into shorter sentences, and say in verse 13 that the cloud came while the music was sounding.

decisions.choice: whatever their division (Balanced); not only those whose group was on duty (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "without keeping to divisions" means (m3). Readable says "made themselves holy" for "consecrated themselves", as in 1 Chronicles 15:12.

records.heading: The cloud fills the house

records.source: וְהַלְוִיִּ֣ם הַמְשֹׁרֲרִ֣ים לְכֻלָּ֡ם לְאָסָ֡ף לְהֵימָ֣ן לִֽ֠ידֻתוּן וְלִבְנֵיהֶ֨ם וְלַאֲחֵיהֶ֜ם מְלֻבָּשִׁ֣ים בּ֗וּץ בִּמְצִלְתַּ֨יִם֙ וּבִנְבָלִ֣ים וְכִנֹּר֔וֹת עֹמְדִ֖ים מִזְרָ֣ח לַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְעִמָּהֶ֤ם כֹּֽהֲנִים֙ לְמֵאָ֣ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֔ים מַחְצְרִ֖ים בַּחֲצֹֽצְרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: and the Levites the singers, all of them, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and their brothers, clothed [in] fine linen, with cymbals and with harps and lyres, standing east of the altar, and with them priests, one hundred and twenty, blowing on trumpets,
pieces: All the Levites who were singers, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun with their sons and relatives, were standing east of the altar, dressed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps and lyres. With them were 120 priests blowing trumpets.

L.12: and the Levites, the singers, all of them, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and their brothers, clothed [in] fine linen, with cymbals and with harps and lyres, [were] standing east of the altar, and with them [were] 120 priests blowing on trumpets,

R.12: All the Levite singers were standing on the east side of the altar. They were Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun and their sons and relatives. They were dressed in fine linen and held cymbals, harps and lyres. With them were 120 priests who played trumpets.

decisions.choice: all of them, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun: the list names who the singers were
decisions.reason: Each name in the list begins with a small word meaning "to" or "belonging to", used here to set out the members of a group, as in 1 Chronicles 25:1-6. It says who the singers were: the three leaders and their families.

decisions.choice: Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun: the leaders of the temple singers David appointed
decisions.reason: David set these three and their sons over the music of worship (1 Chronicles 16:41-42; 25:1-6). Jeduthun is probably the Ethan of 1 Chronicles 15:19.

decisions.choice: clothed in fine linen: dressed for service in worship
decisions.reason: Fine linen was worn by those who served at the sanctuary. The Levites and singers wore it when David brought the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 15:27).

decisions.choice: cymbals, harps and lyres: the instruments of the Levite singers
decisions.reason: The cymbals were a pair of bronze plates struck together; harps and lyres were the two stringed instruments, the harp the larger, as in 1 Chronicles 15:16 and 25:1.

decisions.choice: 120 priests blowing trumpets: the priests' task in worship
decisions.reason: The law gave the trumpets to the priests, to be blown at festivals and offerings (Numbers 10:8-10; 1 Chronicles 15:24; 16:6).

decisions.choice: relatives (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means fellow members of the singers' families, as in 1 Chronicles 15:16.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י כְ֠אֶחָד לַמְחַצְּרִ֨ים וְלַמְשֹֽׁרֲרִ֜ים לְהַשְׁמִ֣יעַ קוֹל־אֶחָ֗ד לְהַלֵּ֣ל וּלְהֹדוֹת֮ לַיהוָה֒ וּכְהָרִ֣ים ק֠וֹל בַּחֲצֹצְר֨וֹת וּבִמְצִלְתַּ֜יִם וּבִכְלֵ֣י הַשִּׁ֗יר וּבְהַלֵּ֤ל לַיהוָה֙ כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְהַבַּ֛יִת מָלֵ֥א עָנָ֖ן בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: and it was, as one, for the trumpeters and for the singers to make heard one voice, to praise and to give thanks to Yahweh, and as raising [the] voice with trumpets and with cymbals and with instruments of the song, and in praising Yahweh, for [he is] good, for to forever [is] his loyal love, and the house was filled [with a] cloud, [the] house of Yahweh,
pieces: The trumpeters and the singers joined as one, making a single sound heard as they praised and thanked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. As they raised the sound with trumpets, cymbals and other musical instruments and praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love lasts forever," the house, the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, was filled with a cloud,

L.13: and it happened, as one, for the trumpeters and for the singers to make one sound heard, to praise and to give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and as [they] raised [the] sound with trumpets and with cymbals and with instruments of song, and praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "For [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is] good, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever," that the house was filled [with] a cloud, the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

R.13: The trumpet players and the singers joined together to praise and thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as if with one voice. They played their trumpets, cymbals and other instruments and praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, singing, "He is good! His faithful love lasts forever." Then the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was filled with a cloud.

decisions.choice: as one ... one sound: in perfect unity
decisions.reason: The verse says twice that the music was one: the trumpeters and singers were "as one", and they made "one sound" heard. The praise of the whole company rose together.

decisions.choice: for he is good, for his loyal love is forever: the refrain of Israel's praise
decisions.reason: These are the words of Psalm 136:1 and 106:1, 107:1 and 118:1, sung when the ark came to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 16:34), sung again when fire fell on the altar (7:3), and at the laying of the second temple's foundation (Ezra 3:11). They are rendered here as in the Psalms.

decisions.choice: loyal love: faithful, covenant love
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith within a bond, here Yahweh's love for his people, as in Psalm 136:1.

decisions.choice: the house was filled with a cloud: told also in 1 Kings 8:10
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 8:10 says "the cloud filled the house of Yahweh", the known cloud of Yahweh's presence (Exodus 40:34). Chronicles says "the house was filled with a cloud, the house of Yahweh", repeating "house" for weight, and lets the cloud come as the praise is sung.

decisions.choice: instruments of song: the instruments used to accompany the singing
decisions.reason: "Instruments of song" is the usual name in Chronicles for the instruments of temple music (1 Chronicles 15:16; 16:42).

decisions.choice: for he is good, for his loyal love is forever (Literal); for he is good; his loyal love lasts forever (Balanced); He is good! His faithful love lasts forever (Readable)
decisions.reason: The refrain is worded as in 1 Chronicles 16:34 and the Psalms it quotes: "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced, "faithful love" at Readable. Every use of the refrain in 2 Chronicles (7:3, 6; 20:21) keeps this wording.

decisions.choice: the house, the house of the LORD (Balanced); the temple of the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Hebrew's repeated "house". Readable says it once, as "the temple", as in 1 Kings 8:10, and begins a new sentence with "Then" since it broke the long sentence of verses 11-13 into shorter ones.

records.source: וְלֹא־יָֽכְל֧וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים לַעֲמ֥וֹד לְשָׁרֵ֖ת מִפְּנֵ֣י הֶעָנָ֑ן כִּֽי־מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: and not were able the priests to stand to minister because of the cloud, for filled [the] glory of Yahweh [the] house of the God.
pieces: and the priests were unable to stand and do their service because of the cloud, since the house of God was full of the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: and the priests were not able to stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} filled the house of God.

R.14: The priests could not stand there to do their work because of the cloud. The glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} filled God's temple.

decisions.choice: told also in 1 Kings 8:11, as at the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The sentence is the same as 1 Kings 8:11, except that Kings ends "the house of Yahweh" and Chronicles "the house of God". Exodus 40:35 says that Moses was not able to enter the tent of meeting, because the cloud had settled on it and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle. 7:1-2 tells of the glory filling the house again after Solomon's prayer.

decisions.choice: the glory of Yahweh: his presence made visible
decisions.reason: The glory is Yahweh himself present among his people. By filling the house he shows that he accepts it as his dwelling, as Solomon's words in the next chapter say (6:1-2).

decisions.choice: to stand to minister: to stay at their posts and serve
decisions.reason: Priests "stand before Yahweh to minister" (Deuteronomy 10:8; 18:5). The cloud made it impossible to remain in their place.

decisions.choice: lowercase "and"; the house was full of the glory (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced continue the sentence of verse 13. Balanced follows the wording of 1 Kings 8:11 and Exodus 40:35.
